You should consider the following

Religion - would you want your kids to learn a particular religion. E.g. Catholic schools teach the bible etc.

Performance - how did the school perform against the state average or other options.

Facilities - I went to a public school and the facilities were extremely limited. This will restrict your child's ability to develop in a speciality area they love. It honestly did change my career choice. And it especially impacted the male students outcome. My public school could only afford pen and paper, and boys perform less well in classes that are taught purely from a text book.

Co-ed? If you have a girl and boy a co-ed school will allow them to study together. Single gender schools are popular as teaching styles will be catered to them and many other reasons.

Teaching staff - meet the staff at the school. It's important that their attitude to education aligns with yours.

Discipline - private schools have much higher discipline and stricter policies.

Programs - what programs do they offer (e.g. Accelerated learning for gifted children, drama, music, sports teams)

Just few of many things to consider.
